vertical_datum_authority: NZVD2016 identity supplied by the model owner for the authorised v0.1 release; no vertical conversion applied.

grid.catchment_scope: Complete established hydraulic model raster and physical mask; not a claim of complete geographical catchment coverage.

processing_history: Original multi-survey LINZ elevation sources and historical hydraulic conditioning retained.
The original conditioned model DEM and benchmark comparison packet agree exactly at every active cell.
No resampling, interpolation, vertical shift or DEM modification during release export.
Only the separately supplied physical mask defines nodata; legitimate low elevations remain active.
Retained south-first solver outputs are explicitly reversed to the original north-first raster orientation.
GeoTIFF FP64 values are losslessly compressed with DEFLATE; conversion error verified per product.

channel_rule.name: windowed_cumulative_net_throughflow
channel_rule.note: event-specific channel rule: the volume threshold is tied to this diagnostic rainfall event and accumulation window; changing the diagnostic rainfall depth/duration or throughflow_window_s may require a different minimum_channel_throughflow_m3
channel_rule.rule: a model cell is a confirmed channel cell when its cumulative net throughflow over the first 24000 s of the diagnostic event reaches 50000 m3

hydraulic_conditioning.hydraulic_conveyance_analysis_extent_war: channel corridors touch the north, south, west, east edge(s) of the hydraulic analysis extent; significant transport across the analysis boundary means the upstream catchment area is truncated. Inward transport is impossible by construction (the boundary faces are one-way outward), so a corridor touching the boundary is always potentially under-fed; treat its effective contributing area as a lower bound conditional on the analysis extent.

71.basis: heavy timber stand (Arcement & Schneider); dense indigenous understorey
71.label: Natural Forest
71.note: tallest, densest NZ class; consider the upper range in old-growth catchments

72.basis: mature exotic plantation, full canopy (Arcement & Schneider timber stands)
72.label: Planted Forest - Pre 1990

73.basis: younger exotic plantation; thinner trunks and more open understorey than pre-1990
73.label: Post 1989 Forest

74.basis: scattered-to-medium brush reversion (Chow flood-plain brush values)
74.label: Grassland - With woody biomass

75.basis: improved pasture ≈ high grass flood plain (Chow 0.035)
75.label: Grassland - High producing

77.basis: perennial woody trunks with canopy; between brush and trees (Chow)
77.label: Cropland - Orchards and vineyards (perennial)

78.basis: cultivated/row-crop flood plain (Chow 0.02-0.04, upper half bare-earth conservative)
78.label: Cropland - Annual

79.label: Wetland - Open water
79.note: where hydraulically significant, channel/lake routing usually dominates a bulk n

80.basis: dense emergent vegetation (raupō/swamp sedge; Chow dense brush 0.10)
80.label: Wetland - Vegetated non forest

81.label: Settlements or built-up area
81.note: weakest class: LUCAS settlements are areal averages; building footprints / DEM conditioning represent urban blockage far better than a blanket n

82.label: Other
82.note: heterogeneous aggregate (beaches, mines, bare ground); review per site

details.coverage_note: LUCAS v003 validated wall-to-wall over NZ land (99.97% of the 150k coastline mask); unmapped cells are offshore or coastal-margin detail.
details.global_notes: Vegetation roughness is depth-dependent (flexible grasses lay down, submerged forest trunks roughen); values are static single-event starting points for calibration, not hydraulic truth.

subid_notes.1001: peat mine: bare/worked surface near the class 82 value
subid_notes.120: shrubland understorey: consider the upper range of class 74
subid_notes.121: tall forest: consider the upper range of class 71
subid_notes.122: wilding trees: between classes 74 and 73 depending on maturity

source_revision_note: Exact runtime module and external binary hashes are preserved in each immutable completed record; the anchor identifies retained completion evidence.
infiltration_equation: f(F) = k + (f0 - k) exp(-F/fd), limited by available water; F is cumulative infiltration depth
